description: Lookup: actor role (docket Section 3). Rows are deactivated (is_active), not deleted, once referenced.
Permission granted to a role (junction, owned by both sides)
Login identity (candidate, recruiter, consultant, admin, system). Stub in Phase 1; extended by Administration in M7-M10
A user (usually a candidate) blocks one user or one organisation; unblocking sets deleted_at so history is kept. RLS in M18 hides the blocker from the blocked party
Consent given or withdrawn; the latest row per user and purpose is the current state (withdrawal is a new row)
Lookup: action a role may perform. Rows are deactivated (is_active), not deleted, once referenced.
Password credential of a login identity: hash only, one per user (owned by app_user). Restricted grants in M18
Role held by a user, optionally scoped to an organisation, over an effective period; revocation closes the period (history kept)
Audit trail of sensitive actions (RG4); application users cannot update or delete it (trigger + revoked grants). Retention: 7 years
System errors (application and integration). Retention: 90 days
Gig worker applies to a gig request; bids flow one way and only the requester decides
Accepted gig application turned into work for a window; fulfilment itself runs in the external system
Time slot a gig worker is available; slots of one worker do not overlap (owned by the worker profile)
Effective-dated charge rate of a service offering; one rate per unit at a time (owned by the offering)
[integration-write] Estimated, projected and total earnings reported by the fulfilment system (source of truth); a newer figure is a new row. The application can only read it
Handoff of an assignment to the external fulfilment system (integration boundary): idempotent send, external reference, status
Requester rating of a completed gig, one per assignment
Short project-based request with a time window and a fixed or rate-based price
Requester favourite or blacklist entry for a worker; a worker is on at most one list per requester (owned by both sides)
Service a gig worker offers, one per skill (owned by the worker profile)
Gig worker profile, separate from candidate profiles (docket Section 2); 1:1 with app_user
Candidate application to a requirement: current status, source, resume, applied_at; one per candidate per job. Retention: anonymised with the profile
Candidate answer to a screening question (owned by the application)
Every application status transition with actor (created_by), time and reason
Legal (from, to) status moves read by trg_application_status_transition
Interview round of an application
One opening within a requirement and its fill state (positions count = rows; owned by the requirement)
Job posting (non-gig categories): owner and client, category, role, salary with disclosure, experience range, lifecycle, publish state, consultant openness
City a requirement is open in (junction, owned by the requirement)
Qualification accepted for a requirement (junction, owned by the requirement)
Questionnaire attached to a requirement (junction, owned by the requirement)
Skill required by a requirement (junction, owned by the requirement)
Each job search run by a candidate or guest (job search history)
Joining against an accepted offer; one per application
Offer made on an application; a revised offer is a new row
Allowed answer of a choice question (owned by the question)
Reusable screening questionnaire owned by an organisation
Ordered question in a questionnaire (owned by the questionnaire)
Candidate saved job search (owned by the candidate); job alerts on it live in Notifications
Named shortlist owned by an organisation (Sourcing references it)
Candidate on a shortlist; removal sets deleted_at so shortlist history (who added, when removed) is kept
Commercial account (customer) that owns one or more organisations, their subscriptions and wallet
User who administers a commercial account (owned by the account); at most one primary
Employer, client, consultancy or campus. Stub in Phase 1; extended by Organisation and account in M7-M10
Tax or registration identifier (GSTIN, PAN, CIN, EIN) of an organisation; written through org.add_identifier, never in clear
Office or site of an organisation (owned by the organisation)
Which organisation a recruiter works for, over which dates; periods for one recruiter never overlap (history kept by closing the period)
One verification request to the company registration / tax service and its outcome (integration boundary, docket Section 6)
Assessment catalogue entry
One submitted assessment attempt with its score; abandoned attempts are not recorded
Candidate activity log: login, profile update, resume download ...
Candidate address (owned by the profile)
Bookmark added or removed by an employer or recruiter (bookmark history)
Certification held by a candidate (owned by the profile)
Email, phone and WhatsApp contact points of a candidate (owned by the profile)
Education history entry (owned by the profile)
National identifier reference from the identity verification service; the raw number is never stored (docket Section 6)
Languages a candidate knows (junction, owned by the profile)
City a candidate wants to work in (junction, owned by the profile)
Job role a candidate is looking for (junction, owned by the profile)

Candidate personal details, headline, summary, experience and salary with disclosure; 1:1 with app_user. Retention: anonymised and purged 30 days after a deletion request, or after 36 months of inactivity
Candidate or gig project with role, duration and outcome (owned by the profile)
Candidate-to-skill junction (owned by the profile)
External profile link (owned by the profile)
Employment history entry (owned by the profile)
Course catalogue entry
Candidate enrolment in a course (owned by the candidate)
Current completion score of a profile (derived, one row per profile, recomputed on change)
Which employer or recruiter viewed which profile, and when (profile view history). Paid views link their ledger debit in M14
Who referred whom, optionally for a job, and how far it progressed (referral tracking and events)
Platform resume layout candidates build from
A saved resume, built from a template or uploaded (owned by the profile)
